chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, who said:

I asked Abd al-Salih (peace be upon him), so I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! We were companions with a people in Mecca, so we departed from them, and we carried some of their goods without knowledge. The people had gone, and we do not know them, nor do we know their homelands. So the goods remained with us, so what shall we do with them?'
He said: 'You carry it until you catch up with them in Al-Kufa.'
Yunus said: 'I said to him, 'I do not know them, and we do not know how to ask about them.''
He said: 'Sell it and give its price to your companions.'
So I said, 'May I be sacrificed for you! The people of Wilayah?'

key_terms.الْوَلَايَةُ: Wilayah (guardianship/authority, referring to the Imams or their deputies)
key_terms.عَبْدٌ صَالِحٌ: Abd al-Salih (a title often used for Imam al-Sadiq in this narration)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on goods left behind by people who departed without notice?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the practical application of *khums* and the authority of the Imams in managing unclaimed property (*al-mal al-mafqud*). It highlights the jurisprudential nuance where, if the original owners are unknown or untraceable, the proceeds from selling their goods are allocated to the 'Ahl al-Wilayah,' affirming the Imams' role as custodians of community wealth in the absence of clear heirs.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Yunus Bin Abdul Rahman who said,

‘I asked Abd Salih<sup>asws</sup> (7<sup>th</sup> Imam<sup>asws</sup>), so I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! We had friends from the people of Makka, so when went away from them, we (found out later that) we were unknowingly carrying some of their goods with us, and the people had gone and we do not recognise them, nor do we recognise their home towns. So the goods remained with us, so what shall we do with these?’
So he (the narrator) said, ‘He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Keep carrying them until you meet them in Al-Kufa’.
So Yunus (the narrator) said, I said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘We do not know them and we do not know how we should be asking around about them’.
So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Sell it and give its price to your companions’.
So I said, ‘May I be sacrificed for you<sup>asws</sup>! The people of your<sup>asws</sup> Wilayah?’
en.sarwar: 22. Ali has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from Yunus ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman who has said the following:

“This is concerning my question before the virtuous servant of Allah saying, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, we in Makkah had travel-mates, and when they left and we also left we carried certain items of their goods without knowing and they had gone. We did not know their places and the goods were left with us. What should we do about them?
He (the Imam) said, ‘Take them with you to meet them in al-Kufah.’
I (Yunus) said, ‘I do not know them and we do not know how to find them.’
He (the Imam) said, ‘Sell the items and give its price to your people.’
I then asked, ‘I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause, should I give them to Ahl al-Walayah (people who believe in the Divine Authority of ‘A’immah)?
He (the Imam) said, ‘Yes, give it to them.’”
